title: 多进程架构的内存收益、账单代价与 lmkd 风险
key_conclusions: Multi-process architecture must be evaluated by total scenario memory, not by main-process PSS alone.
Zygote and dex/oat mappings can be shared, but Java heap, native heap, caches, and SDK initialization often duplicate.
lmkd risk expands because each process has its own oom_score_adj, restart behavior, and victim-benefit profile.
A process split is useful on low-end devices only when it shifts or caps memory away from a critical user-visible window.
shallow_points: The article does not include measured single-process versus multi-process traces.
It does not validate ActivityManager OomAdjuster behavior against a specific Android branch.
It does not include real memcg samples from multiple app processes.
It does not quantify Binder and dma-buf costs for common split-process patterns.
discovered_connections: Day 70's per-window peak model is needed to decide whether process splitting moves memory away from a scroll or launch critical window.
Day 67's memcg boundary prevents treating cgroup charge as producer proof.
Day 68's cross-validation is required when per-process PSS disagrees with mappings, heapprofd, or shared fd evidence.
Day 72 should connect R8 and dex/class loading to duplicated per-process startup and runtime costs.
suggest_future_topics: Day 72 should focus on ProGuard/R8 effects on dex, class loading, JIT, and runtime memory.
A future lab should compare the same feature implemented as one process versus two processes.
A future tool should sum PSS, memcg charge, fd owners, and oom_score_adj across all package processes.
A future case should analyze restart storms after lmkd kills a remote service process.
knowledge_gaps: Need real multi-process meminfo, smaps, memcg, and lmkd traces.
Need branch-specific validation for OomAdjuster and service binding adj propagation.
Need quantified duplicate cache and SDK initialization costs.
Need Binder/dma-buf examples where killing a consumer process fails to release the producer-owned buffer.
